input.title: BH | Premier Matlock Leather Chesterfield Sofa — In Cognac
input.descriptionHtml:
Matlock sits where the Derbyshire Peak drops into the Derwent valley, an old spa town where walkers come back from the hills muddy, cold and very ready to sit down. This sofa is made for that first sinking in. Its seat is 22 inches deep and cushioned with foam, fibre and feather, so it gives as you settle, and its deep-buttoned leather arms rise level with the back to wrap the whole sofa around you.

The leather is top grain and aniline dyed, so its natural grain shows through and it softens with every year of use. The sofa stands on wooden legs fitted with casters, so it can be rolled out to clean beneath or to rearrange the room. It needs some assembly on arrival.

Face it toward the fire in a living room or den, with a wool throw over one arm, a low table before it for tea and the walking maps, and a lamp behind. This listing is for one sofa.

input.title: BH | Premier Jermyn Leather Chesterfield Sofa — In Chestnut
input.descriptionHtml:
Around Jermyn Street, in the old club quarter of St James's in London, the best part of the afternoon is spent in deep leather: a newspaper, a pot of tea, and a long conversation that nobody is rushing. This sofa brings that unhurried hour home. Its rolled arms are shaped for leaning into, its pleated arm fronts and top grain leather have the look of a club room, and at more than eight feet long it has room to stretch out after dinner.

The leather is buttoned deep across the back and over the arms in the traditional Chesterfield way, so the whole sofa reads as one sculpted piece, and it stands low on rubberwood legs. The long seat has room for everyone once the plates are cleared, and the leather softens and gains character the more it is used. Light assembly is required.

Set it facing the fireplace in a den or library, or along the longest wall of a living room, with a low table in front for the papers, a lamp at one end and a wool throw over the arm. This listing is for one sofa.

On the Strand, between the West End theatres and the grand hotels that opened there in the late 1800s, an evening often begins in a hotel lounge, sunk into deep leather with a cocktail before the curtain goes up. This sofa is made for that kind of lingering. Its tufted back and arms stand at one height, so it reads as a single block of leather, and its deep seat holds you comfortably through a whole cocktail and the talk that goes with it.

It is upholstered in top grain aniline leather, dyed right through so it softens and deepens with every year of use, and buttoned in the traditional tufted way. Under the leather, its 22-inch-deep seat is filled with a blend of foam, fiber and feather, and casters under the wooden legs let it be drawn up to the fire. At more than seven feet long it seats a small party, and it needs light assembly.

Place it opposite the fireplace in a living room or library, with the cocktail tray on a low table before it, a lamp beside each arm and a pair of club chairs across from it. This listing is for one sofa.

The sofa arrives fully assembled.

Put it before a fireplace or against the main living room wall, with a coffee table for the programs and the glasses, a reading lamp beside it and a pair of armchairs drawn up opposite. This listing is for one sofa.

Ostend, the Belgian seaside town the painter James Ensor called home, is made for long walks on the promenade in the wind, followed by an afternoon stretched out indoors with the salt still on your skin. This sofa is made for that stretching out. Its seat runs 82 inches long and 26 inches deep, room enough to lie full length with a book or to sit back with your feet tucked under you.

Set it facing the fireplace or a big window in a living room, with a long low table in front for coffee and books, a wool throw folded at one end and a lamp at the other. This listing is for one sofa.

Place it opposite the hearth in a living room or den, with a long coffee table in front for books and mugs, a wool blanket over one arm and a lamp at each end. This listing is for one sofa.

Keep it in a dining room as a drink cart with Madeira, port and a row of small glasses, or roll it beside the table to serve dessert and coffee. This listing is for one serving cart.

The drawers suit flatware and table linens, and the doors take the bigger serving pieces. More than seven feet long, it arrives fully assembled.

Give it the long wall of the dining room, with a lamp at each end, a cheese board and a carafe on top, and the good tablecloths folded away in the drawers below. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Seven Dials Narrow Six-Door Sideboard
input.descriptionHtml:
Seven Dials sits at the heart of London's theatre district, and an evening there often ends back at home with a late supper laid out for whoever came along. This sideboard is made for serving that supper. At eight feet long it holds the whole spread in one line, from the cheese board to the coffee pot, and at only 12 inches deep it fits a narrow dining room or a hall where a standard sideboard would never go.

It is acacia, a dense hardwood, with six doors finished in raised panels and the same detail carried along its sides, and inside are three shelves that lift out to fit tall jugs and stacks of plates. The doors open the full length of the piece, so the serving dishes are never more than a step away.

Run it along a dining room wall or a narrow hall, with platters, a cake stand and the coffee things on top, and glasses, napkins and serving dishes behind the doors, ready for the next late supper after a show. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Rouen Acacia Sideboard
input.descriptionHtml:
In the half-timbered houses of old Rouen, breakfast is a bowl of milky coffee, bread from the bakery and Normandy butter, set out on the sideboard for whoever comes down first. This sideboard is made for that easy morning spread. Its broad top holds the coffee pot, the bread board and a jar of jam, and its three top drawers keep napkins, spoons and butter knives exactly where you reach for them.

It is built of acacia, a dense hardwood with a strong, lively grain, and below the drawers three adjustable shelves can be set to fit tall jugs, stacked bowls or boxes of cereal. A keyhole plate, called an escutcheon, is there for looks alone and gives the front an old French charm. At 36 inches high it doubles as a serving counter. It arrives fully assembled.

Put it in a kitchen or breakfast room with a coffee maker, a fruit bowl and a stack of everyday plates, or in a dining room for linens and serving dishes. This listing is for one sideboard.

Stand it against the long wall of the dining room, with tall candlesticks, a tray of glasses and a bowl of winter fruit on top, and the good china and table linens stored inside. This listing is for one sideboard.

At more than six and a half feet wide it gives a long, unbroken run of storage along a dining or living-room wall. It arrives fully assembled.

Run it along the dining-room wall with a pair of lamps and a bowl of lemons, a cheese board and a row of wine glasses out on top, and plates and linens stored below. This listing is for one sideboard.

Its long top holds the roast, the vegetables and the gravy boat, and its mix of doors and drawers keeps the carving set, the serving spoons and the good plates ready.

It is built from reclaimed pine and finished by hand, so the old timber's grain and character come through. At just over six feet long and 33 inches high, it gives a dining room a generous run of serving space at a comfortable height for carving. Behind the doors there is room for the roasting pans and the big serving platters. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it on the main dining room wall with a pair of lamps and a framed print above, the roasting dishes on top, and the table linens kept in the drawers until Sunday. This listing is for one sideboard.

This sideboard is made for that kind of hungry, crowded supper. Eight feet long, it takes a whole meal set out for everyone to help themselves, and its row of doors opens onto deep storage for casseroles, platters and table linen.

It is built of pine, and each door carries carved detail, a country touch that gives the long front its rhythm. Inside, three shelves lift out, so you can make room for a stockpot or a tall stack of serving platters. At 39 inches tall it is a comfortable height for serving.

Set it along a dining room or kitchen wall with a pair of lamps, a bowl of apples and a stack of plates ready for supper, or use it in a family room for games and glasses. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Lechlade Reclaimed Pine Sideboard
input.descriptionHtml:
In the honey-coloured stone houses of Lechlade, where the Thames first becomes navigable, supper is simple and the dishes are set out on the side for everyone to help themselves. This sideboard is made for that kind of easy supper in a smaller room. At under five feet wide and only 16 inches deep it fits a cottage dining room, a bedroom or an entry hall, and its finish is rubbed by hand, so the reclaimed pine beneath shows its age and grain.

It is built of reclaimed pine, wood saved from earlier use, which gives every piece its own knots and marks, and its top stands 36 inches high, a comfortable height for setting dishes down and serving from. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it in a small dining room with a lamp, a bread board and a jug of flowers on top, or in a hall as a place for gloves, letters and keys, with a mirror hung above it. This listing is for one sideboard.

In Roundstone, the fishing village on the Connemara coast, supper is whatever came in on the boats that day, served at a big kitchen table with the harbour just outside the window. This sideboard is made for that kind of supper, when the plates come out of one place and the forks out of another. Its three drawers keep flatware and linen in order, and behind its four doors there is room for every dish the table could need.

It is built from reclaimed pine, with a diamond shape set into every door, carved detail around the drawers and bun feet, small flattened ball feet, beneath. Behind the doors are three shelves in all that lift out, so the space can be set for tall pitchers or stacks of bowls. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it against the kitchen or dining room wall with a lamp, a stack of plates and a pitcher of wildflowers on top, and table linens, flatware and serving bowls inside, or use it in a hall for gloves, hats and dog leashes. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Gubbio Two-Door Sideboard — In Amber
input.descriptionHtml:
In the stone houses of Gubbio, the medieval town on the slopes of Monte Ingino in Umbria, lunch is a family affair, carried from the stove to a table close by and served without ceremony. This small sideboard is made for that kind of easy serving. At just under four feet wide it fits where a long buffet will not, and its two doors keep the dishes and the wine within arm's reach of the table.

It is built from reclaimed pine, timber that has already lived one life and carries the marks of it, with a top left in natural old pine so its grain and age show, and behind the doors is a shelf that lifts out to make room for tall bottles. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a dining nook or at the end of a kitchen with a bowl of lemons, a bread board and a lamp on top, or in a hall or small apartment as a home for glasses and bottles. This listing is for one sideboard.

This sideboard is made for serving a dinner like that. Running more than eight feet, it has space to set out every dish along its top, and its doors keep everything needed to serve it close at hand.

Behind them are three shelves that lift out, so the space can be set for tall decanters or stacked plates, and the reclaimed timber brings the warmth of age. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it the long wall of a dining room, with tall candlesticks at either end and the serving dishes lined up down the middle, or use it in a living room to hold glasses, bottles and a bowl of lemons. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Èze Four-Door Reclaimed Pine Sideboard
input.descriptionHtml:
Èze is perched on a rock high above the Mediterranean, and a Riviera dinner there is taken slowly, on a terrace with the sea going dark below and dish after dish coming out of the kitchen. This sideboard is made for keeping that kind of meal flowing. Its four doors hide the plates, glasses and bottles for a long dinner, and its top runs nearly seven feet, room enough to lay out each course as it arrives.

It is built of reclaimed pine, with four doors set between plain upright stiles, the vertical posts of the frame. Three removable shelves inside can be lifted out to fit large platters or a stack of serving bowls. It arrives fully assembled.

Place it in a dining room or a big kitchen, with a lamp, a stack of white plates and a bowl of lemons on top, and a carafe of rosé chilling for the first course, and the wine, linens and serving dishes inside. This listing is for one sideboard.

This demilune cabinet is made to stand at the side of that supper, holding what the table needs next. Its three doors open onto three shelves for the plates, glasses and bottles of a supper party, and its curved front lets guests pass close by on the way to the table.

Demilune means half-moon: it is straight at the back and curved at the front, so it sits snug against a wall with no corners to catch a hip. It is built of pine in a hand-rubbed finish. At 45 inches tall it stands higher than a sideboard, a good height to serve from or to raise a lamp toward eye level. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it in a dining room between two windows with a lamp and a bowl of fruit on top, or in an entry hall with a vase of flowers and a dish for keys, the doors hiding everything else. This listing is for one cabinet.

This sideboard is made for serving that supper. Its long top holds the pie dish, the bread and the jug of gravy, and its four doors carry a pie-crust detail, the decorative edging long associated with eighteenth-century English tea tables.

It is built of pine in a softly worn finish, and inside, two removable shelves can be set for stacks of plates or lifted out for tall platters. At 22 inches deep there is room inside for the big serving dishes, the roasting pans and the cake stand, and it arrives fully assembled.

Use it in a dining room or a farmhouse kitchen with a lamp, a bowl of apples and a cake under a glass dome, or in an upstairs hall for linens and spare blankets. This listing is for one sideboard.

At 78 inches wide it holds every dish before it goes to the table, the salad, the bread, the pitcher of water and the wine, and its doors, trimmed with arches, keep the plates and glasses close.

It is pine in a washed finish with an aged look, and the arches are applied to the door fronts, giving them the outline of old church windows. Behind the doors are two shelves that lift out, so tall pitchers and big serving bowls have room, and the low, wide top is an easy height for serving from. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it under a window or against the long wall of the dining room, with a bowl of oranges and a big ceramic platter on top and the everyday plates, linen and glasses inside. This listing is for one sideboard.

After a day on the slopes above Kitzbühel, supper in a Tyrolean chalet often begins with a small glass of schnapps, poured from a bottle kept somewhere special. This small cabinet is that somewhere. Only 7 inches deep, it holds a few bottles and glasses in a slim space by the dining table, and it has the look of the antique cabinets found in old Tyrolean houses.

It is solid acacia, a dense, hardwearing timber, finished warm and soft so the grain glows. An iron key turns in an escutcheon, the decorative plate around a keyhole, a detail taken from antique Alpine pieces, so the bottle inside stays where it belongs. At 27 inches wide and 35 tall it fits a narrow wall beside a doorway or between two windows, where a deeper piece would be in the way. It arrives fully assembled.

Stand it against a dining room or hall wall, with a bottle of schnapps and a few small glasses inside and a candle on top. This listing is for one cabinet.

This sideboard is made for dinners with that sense of occasion. Its three doors keep the good china and silver close to the table, ready to come out course by course, and its top stands at a comfortable height to serve from.

It is made of wood, with applied moulding framing a panel on each of the three doors, each fitted with a keyhole plate and a key that doubles as a pull, and touches of gold across the front. Inside, two adjustable shelves fit platters and stacks of plates, and at five feet long it sits comfortably in a smaller dining room. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it along a dining room wall beneath a gilt mirror, with candlesticks and a tureen on top and silver, linens and the best glasses inside, or use it in a hall for gloves and scarves. This listing is for one sideboard.

On Bornholm, the Danish island far out in the Baltic, winter evenings are long and dark, and they are spent at home with a film, a fire and a plate of smoked herring from one of the island's smokehouses. This low console is made for those nights in. It stands just 22 inches high, a comfortable height to set a television on, and behind its doors two removable shelves keep the films, games and cables out of sight.

It is reclaimed pine, so the timber carries the marks of an earlier life, under a washed finish, with a pine top in a contrasting finish. The detailed doors give the front its character. At 71 inches long it gives a wide television room to sit with a speaker at each side, and at 17 inches deep it keeps close to the wall. It arrives fully assembled.

Set it under a wall-mounted television or with one on top, in a den or living room, with a lamp, a stack of records and a bowl of candles. This listing is for one media console.

This sideboard is made for serving a meal like that. Its top keeps the bread board, the crock and the wine a step from the table, and behind its four doors there is room for every plate and glass.

It is pine, built as a breakfront, a centre section that steps forward from the sides, which gives a plain dining room a sense of architecture. At 63 inches wide and 40 high it is a practical size, generous inside but easy to place, and it arrives fully assembled.

Keep it near the table with a lamp, a bread board and a bowl of cherries on top, and plates, glasses and table linens stored inside, or in a living room as a bar with the bottles behind the doors. This listing is for one sideboard.

At Cheverny in the Loire, the château still keeps its pack of hounds and its painted rooms, and the dining room belongs to a tradition of grand tables after the hunt. This cabinet is made for a dining room in that spirit, where the silver, the good china and the bottles saved for guests need a worthy home. A full eight feet long, it gives a whole service its own place, and its four doors keep the best things in order between occasions.

It is made in Italy from solid pine, and each of its four doors carries a neoclassical emblem with an aged brass escutcheon, a decorative metal plate set into the door front, and a key that serves as its pull. Behind the doors, four adjustable shelves can be set to fit tall decanters or stacks of plates. It arrives fully assembled.

Let it fill the long wall of a dining room, with a pair of candelabra, a large painting above and a bowl of fruit at the centre, the shelves inside holding china, silver and linens. This listing is for one cabinet.

input.title: BH | Premier Montsoreau Four-Door Reclaimed Pine Sideboard — In Driftwood
input.descriptionHtml:
In Montsoreau, the tufa-stone village where the Vienne meets the Loire, supper comes with a bottle of Saumur-Champigny and something slow-cooked, served from the side of the room. This sideboard is made for that serving. Its top runs seven and a half feet, room for the casserole, the bread, the cheese and the wine side by side, and four doors keep the dishes and glasses close.

It is reclaimed pine, finished in two tones so the doors stand out gently from the case around them, and two removable shelves inside let you set the spacing for tall bottles or stacks of plates. Each door opens from a simple hand hold rather than a knob, which keeps the fronts clean. The reclaimed pine brings warmth and a little history to a formal room. It arrives fully assembled.

Run it down the long wall of a dining room, a large mirror hung above and a lamp at each end, with a carafe of wine and a cheese board waiting on top. This listing is for one sideboard.

input.title: BH | Premier Harewood Walnut Burl Sideboard — In Chestnut
input.descriptionHtml:
Thomas Chippendale's workshop made furniture for Harewood House in Yorkshire through the 1770s, among it fine veneered pieces for the dining room, where dinner was laid out and served from long sideboards. This sideboard carries that tradition of fine veneer into the modern dining room, made for the business of serving a dinner. At 80 inches long its top takes the whole meal in one line, from the carving board to the coffee, and the space below keeps the good china within reach of the table.

It is built from maple with quarter-sawn walnut and walnut burl veneers, burl being the swirling figure cut from a growth on the trunk, and its panels are bookmatched, two leaves of veneer opened like a book so their grain mirrors. Mitred corners and smoothly planed surfaces finish it, with aged brass hardware. It arrives fully assembled.

Give it the wall opposite the windows in a dining room, with a decanter, a pair of candlesticks and a bowl of fruit on top, and the china, silver and table linens inside. This listing is for one sideboard.
